summary: After the Wallabies' historic first World Cup pool exit, the Queensland Rugby Union (QRU) backed a fully independent review of the Wallabies program and reaffirmed support for centralised high-performance but refused to hand commercial functions to Rugby Australia, unlike the NSW Waratahs. The QRU's open letter also asked RA to reinstate $1.7m annual funding to Super Rugby franchises. The article also covers RA's finances, loan plans and broadcast deal hopes.
one_line: The QRU backs a Wallabies review and high-performance centralisation but refuses to give Rugby Australia its commercial operations, after the Waratahs handed over their licence.
key_facts: The QRU backs a 'fully independent and transparent top-to-bottom review of the Wallabies program' after the Wallabies' historic first World Cup pool exit.
The QRU wants RA to reinstate the annual $1.7 million funding to each Super Rugby franchise that was withdrawn after the Covid pandemic.
QRU chief executive David Hanham and chairman Brett Clark sent an open letter to members on Wednesday morning.
The QRU letter states it 'will not agree to any proposal on centralising commercial or corporate functions'.
The QRU supports centralisation including a national player-contracting model and alignment of coaching, strength and conditioning, and medical staff.
The NSW Waratahs, on the brink of insolvency, are handing their licence, commercial and high-performance operations to RA, to be run out of RA's office; Paul Doorn informed stakeholders.
The Melbourne Rebels are expected to follow the Waratahs; the ACT Brumbies, like the QRU, don't want to give up commercial assets.
Les Kiss was appointed Reds coach, replacing Brad Thorn, with RA involved in the appointment.
The QRU says it has delivered four straight operating profits and helped deliver $31 million of improvements to Ballymore via the National Rugby Training Centre.
The QRU cites 71,000 players in Queensland, over 16,000 of them female, and 257 schools with rugby programs.
RA took a $40m loan from Ares, has about $15m left, and is looking to borrow up to another $60m.
RA hopes to at least double its broadcast deal with Nine Entertainment/Stan Sport, currently $29m per year until the end of 2025.
Eddie Jones said Australian rugby has fallen behind and needs a centralised model to develop more and better players.
